questions.question: Why is $\sigma=0$ excluded from the normal distribution definition?
options: The mean would no longer be real
The exponential function would disappear, no matter which values are selected.
The density formula requires a positive spread parameter
questions.explanation: The normal density divides by $\sigma$ and uses $(x-\mu)^2/\sigma^2$, so it requires a positive spread parameter $\sigma>0$.
questions.source_support: The definition explicitly requires $\sigma>0$.
questions.polish_notes: Quality round 9: rebalanced correct-answer positions to remove option-index guessing cue
option_explanations: $\sigma=0$ does not affect whether the mean is real.
A finite support is not the reason; the density formula itself needs $\sigma>0$.
The exponential function does not 'disappear'; the issue is division by $\sigma$.
